question: Why a country whose land draws on nothing books supplies as traded away in a new game's second day.

slots_noted.0xEF7C0: Already recorded; this revises the comment only.
slots_noted.0x1BB950: Already recorded; this revises the comment only.

addresses.name: CCountry::IsFriend
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CCountry::IsFriend(CCountry* this, const CCountryTag* tag, bool includeMilitaryAccess)
addresses.comment:
**The game's own name, out of the Lua API (`CCountry:IsFriend`).** `ret 8`, 75 callers; read whole, 0x4EF7C0..0x4EF933. True, in order, when: the tag is this country; the other country's Overlord (+0xF38/+0xF3C) is this country, or this country's Overlord is the other; both have the same non-null Overlord; this country's faction (+0xD8) is real (its slot 7) and is the other's faction; **the other country's** diplomacy status toward this one (`countries[tag]->+0xE28[this->id]`) has an alliance (+0x14); or that status is co_belligerent (+0x58) and this country is not its enemy (CCountry::IsEnemyTag); or, only with includeMilitaryAccess, **this country's** status toward the other has hasMilitaryAccess (+0x4C). False otherwise. Espionage passes true in CSpyPresence::CatchSpies (a friend's spies are not caught, a hostile friend's at home are certain to pass the first roll) and false in CSpyPresence::IsHostileMission (counter-espionage in a friend is benign). CAIUnit slot 76 uses it with true to skip any plan objective in friendly-controlled territory.

**The null country is a friend of every country with no overlord** (read 2026-11-19, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplypass.md, section 4): the second arm compares `countries[tag.id]->+0xF3C` - the other's overlord id - with `this->+0xCA8`, and a country with no overlord holds 0 there, the null country's id (0x4EF7F9-0x4EF80F). So `countries[0]->IsFriend(anyone unsubjected)` is true. It matters where a caller asks it of a province's controller and the province is province 0, whose controller id is 0: ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel's depot test for ground that draws on nothing.
addresses.evidence: The listing at VA 0x4EF7C0-0x4EF80F; CCountryTag::GetCountry (0x402610) is countries_first[id].
addresses.revises: comment - the null country is a friend of every country with no overlord

addresses.name: CUnit::ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel
addresses.comment:
**One unit's day at the supplies.** It asks CUnit::SupplyConsumption and CUnit::FuelConsumption what the unit uses. In arcade mode it takes that straight out of its country's stockpile. Otherwise it draws on **a province**: the one the unit is in - its owner's acting capital where it is in none - or, where it has a home base (+0x98), the base's, wherever the unit is; an air unit based on a carrier takes the carrier's own base's. `need` is that province's (+0x244) and depot the province its supply_depot_id names. Where the depot's controller is not the payer (the expeditionary owner, else the owner) but is its friend, the payer **pays**: price = (1000 - full) x 250 / 1000 + 1000 with full = pool x 1000 / (SUPPLYPOOL_DAYS x need), 1000 where there is no need, for supplies and fuel apart; price x asked is added to the payer's TradedAway, moved from its stockpile to the depot holder's as far as it has it, and added to the holder's TradedFor and unit_demand. A fleet under a rebase order (0x6DE) has province and depot replaced by its owner's capital after that. Where there is a depot and its controller is no friend of the unit's owner both received figures are 0 and nothing more happens. Then: have = the province's pool, and where that is under `need`, have x (asked x 1000 / need) / 1000 - the unit's share of what there is - **where `need` is nought the share is -1, the fixed-point division by nought inlined (0x5BC0AA), so a pool below nought gives have = -pool / 1000, truncated: nearly nothing, and no fault**; received = 1000 and all taken where that covers what was asked, else have x 1000 / asked (-1 where nought was asked, the same guard at 0x5BC10F) and `have` taken. Without a friend's payment what was asked is the unit_demand of **whoever controls the province drawn on**. The take is that country's `usage` only where the unit stands in its acting capital. **Fuel is worked out the same but only taken, and only counted as usage, for a unit that is moving or a fleet away from its base.** Last, the red mark on the counters of the player's own units. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplypass.md, section 4.

**Ground that draws on nothing is paid for** (read 2026-11-19, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplypass.md, section 4): the depot is `provinces[province +0x48]`, province 0 where there is none; the paying test (0x5BBD5C-0x5BBD98) asks only that the depot's controller id (+0x338) is not the payer's (+0xCA8), that `GetCountry(depot +0x334)->IsFriend(payer, true)` - `countries[0]`, the null country, for province 0, a friend of every country with no overlord (CCountry::IsFriend) - and that the payer is no exile. So such a unit pays at the friend's price into the null country's stockpile, its payment booked as TradedAway (and so in CDistributeSupply::GetNeeded) and not as unit_demand; the later depot test is skipped for province 0, and the province's pool gives the unit what it holds. Measured: BlackICE GitHub's new game of 1936, Shanxi (CSX), whose government sits in China's Beiping through the two days and whose land draws on nothing, writes traded_away supplies 1.701 and fuel 0.065 and no supplies in its stockpile; OpenHOI3, given the rule, gives all three.
addresses.evidence: The listing at VA 0x5BBD20-0x5BBD98; BlackICE GitHub's Ireland1936_01_01_00.hoi3, CSX's traded_away and pool, set beside OpenHOI3's firstdays with the rule built, 2026-11-19.
addresses.revises: comment - ground with no depot pays the null country
